world_behind.title: The sermon turns to the Lamanites
world_behind.text: After two chapters about Nephite sin and the signs, verses 4 through 16 are about Samuel's own people.

world_behind.title: Chastening is explained as love
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says the Nephites were chosen and loved, and chastened in their iniquities because he loves them.

world_behind.title: The record's harshest word about the Lamanites appears here
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says the Lord hated their deeds, and gives the cause as the tradition of their fathers.

world_behind.title: They are described by their fear of sinning
world_behind.text: Verse 9 says they will be trodden down and slain rather than take up the buried weapons.

world_behind.title: A restoration is promised
world_behind.text: Verses 11 through 13 cite Zenos and other prophets on the Lamanites returning to the knowledge of their Redeemer.

world_behind.title: The comparison is about opportunity
world_behind.text: Verse 15 says that if the mighty works shown to the Nephites had been shown to them, they would never have dwindled again.

world_behind.title: The chapter ends with two divine sentences
world_behind.text: Verse 16 promises not to destroy the Lamanites utterly, and verse 17 promises to destroy the Nephites utterly if they will not repent.

words.text: Nursing at the breast. The record uses the word twice, at 1 Nephi 17:2 of the women in the wilderness and here. Matthew 24:19 pairs it with being with child in the same kind of warning.
Extended in duration. The record uses the word nine times, three of them in this chapter at verses 4, 10, and 11. Each time it describes days granted to the Lamanites.
Carefully, watching all around. Treated at Mosiah 26:37, of the church under Alma. The record uses it three times, twice in these two chapters, and the King James Bible once, at Ephesians 5:15.

Not tiring. The word occurs once in the record, here, of Lamanite missionary diligence. Helaman 10:4 had used the related "unwearyingness" of Nephi, and the two are the record's only uses of the idea.
Given light or understanding. Treated at Alma 24:30, of people who had been enlightened and then fell away. The record uses it three times. Verse 10 makes it the moment their firmness begins.
One who keeps a flock. The record uses the word twenty-two times, often of Christ, as at Alma 5:38. Verse 13 calls him their great and true shepherd and puts them among his sheep.

phrases.term: Your houses shall be left unto you desolate
phrases.text: The sentence Matthew 23:38 gives in the singular at Jerusalem. Samuel opens the chapter with it, conditioned on repentance.

phrases.term: Wo unto them which are with child, for they shall be heavy and cannot flee
phrases.text: The cost named in the most specific terms available. Verse 2 makes the flight itself the danger.

phrases.term: In the days of their iniquities hath he chastened them because he loveth them
phrases.text: The reason given for the Nephite history the reader has just watched. Chastening is presented as the treatment given to a chosen people.

phrases.term: For this intent hath the Lord prolonged their days
phrases.text: The purpose behind Lamanite survival. Salvation came to them through Nephite preaching, and the extension of their days is tied to it.

phrases.term: They do walk circumspectly before God
phrases.text: Samuel's summary of most of his own nation. Verse 5 lists commandments, statutes, and judgments according to the law of Moses.
What the converted Lamanites do with their conversion. They work to bring the rest of their people to the truth, and the numbers grow daily.

phrases.term: Which faith and repentance bringeth a change of heart unto them
phrases.text: The sequence stated in one clause: scripture, faith, repentance, changed heart. Mosiah 5:2 had described the same thing from the inside.

phrases.term: They fear to take them up lest by any means they should sin
phrases.text: The buried weapons described by the emotion behind them. Verse 9 says they will be trodden down and slain rather than reach for them.

phrases.term: Because of their firmness when they are once enlightened
phrases.text: The quality the promise rests on. What counts is what they do after they believe.

phrases.term: Their great and true shepherd, and be numbered among his sheep
phrases.text: The end of the restoration prophecy. The knowledge they return to is named as knowledge of a person.

phrases.term: In the day of my wisdom they shall return again unto me
phrases.text: The Lord's word about the Lamanites, in the middle of a sermon to Nephites. The timing is left with him.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: Desolate houses
verses.text: Without repentance their houses will be left desolate, their nursing women will have cause to mourn, and those with child will be too heavy to flee and will be trodden down. Wo to the people of Nephi if they do not repent when they see the signs, for they have been a chosen people whom the Lord loved and chastened in their iniquities because he loves them.

verses.label: v. 4–6
verses.title: The Lamanites now
verses.text: He says the Lord hated their deeds because of the tradition of their fathers, and that salvation came to them through Nephite preaching, which is why their days were prolonged. The more part of them walk circumspectly and keep the law of Moses, and they strive with unwearied diligence to bring the rest to the truth, so their numbers grow daily.

verses.label: v. 7–9
verses.title: What conversion did
verses.text: The Nephites have witnessed it: those brought to the truth, taught the wickedness of their fathers' traditions, and led to believe the scriptures come to faith and repentance and a change of heart. They are firm and steadfast. They have buried their weapons and fear to take them up lest they sin, choosing to be trodden down and slain rather than lift a sword, because of their faith in Christ.

verses.label: v. 10–13
verses.title: Prolonged and restored
verses.text: Because of that steadfastness and firmness once enlightened, the Lord will bless them and prolong their days even in iniquity, and even if they dwindle in unbelief, until the restoration spoken of by Zenos and other prophets. In the latter times the promises are extended to them, and through afflictions, driving, hunting, smiting, and scattering, the Lord will be merciful, and they will be brought to the knowledge of their Redeemer and true shepherd and numbered among his sheep.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: Better for them
verses.text: It will be better for them than for the Nephites without repentance, because if the mighty works shown to the Nephites had been shown to the Lamanites, they would never have dwindled in unbelief again.

verses.label: v. 16–17
verses.title: The two sentences
verses.text: The Lord says he will not utterly destroy the Lamanites, and that in the day of his wisdom they will return. Concerning the Nephites, if they will not repent and do his will he will utterly destroy them for their unbelief despite the mighty works done among them, and as surely as the Lord lives it shall be.

chapter.title: A Lamanite preaches to Nephites about Lamanites
chapter.text: Ten of the seventeen verses describe his own people, offered to an audience that had held them in contempt.

chapter.title: Chastening is defined as evidence of love
chapter.text: Verse 3 makes the Nephite afflictions a mark of being chosen. The whole cycle of Helaman 11 is reread in one clause.

chapter.title: Their conversion is measured by what they will not do
chapter.text: Verse 9 describes the buried weapons and the willingness to die rather than dig them up. The test is a refusal.

chapter.title: Firmness after belief is what the promise rests on
chapter.text: Verse 10 commends steadfastness once enlightened. Speed of conversion is not the quality named.

chapter.title: The restoration is placed in the latter times
chapter.text: Verses 11 through 13 promise scattering and mercy together, and cite Zenos as the source.

chapter.title: The comparison is about what each was shown
chapter.text: Verse 15 makes the Nephites more accountable because they saw more. The measure is opportunity rather than performance.

chapter.title: The same phrase runs both ways
chapter.text: Verse 16 has "I will not utterly destroy them" and verse 17 has "I will utterly destroy them," of two peoples, in consecutive verses.

chapter.title: The sermon ends on the Nephites
chapter.text: After ten verses of praise for the Lamanites, the last word is a conditional threat to the audience standing below the wall.

applications.title: Read correction as attention
applications.text: Samuel says the chastening was because they were loved. Being left alone entirely is the worse outcome.

applications.title: Praise the people your audience looks down on
applications.text: He spent most of his sermon describing Lamanite faithfulness to Nephites. Naming someone else's virtue is a way of telling the truth about your own audience.

applications.title: Judge a conversion by what it will not do
applications.text: They feared to pick up a weapon. Look for the thing a change of heart makes unthinkable rather than the thing it makes enthusiastic.

applications.title: Account for what you were given
applications.text: The comparison turned on what each people had been shown. Measure yourself against your own opportunity.

questions.text: What correction in my life came from someone who loved me?
Whose steady faithfulness have I dismissed because of where they came from?
What am I striving at with unwearied diligence?
When did my heart actually change, and what led to it?
What have I buried that I still fear to pick up?
Am I firm after I am convinced, or only while convinced?
What have I been shown that I have not acted on?
